verdict.evidenceQuote: "By default, Claude reads `AGENTS.md` only when you have no `CLAUDE.md` in your working directory or above it. Here's which of your files count for that check: * **Count, so Claude reads them instead of `AGENTS.md`**: a `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or `CLAUDE.local.md` in your working directory or any directory above it * **Don't count, and keep loading alongside `AGENTS.md`**: your `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, your organization's managed `CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/rules/` files" ... "Reading `AGENTS.md` directly requires Claude Code v2.1.277 or later." ... "`claude-md-or-agents-md` | Your `CLAUDE.md` files, or your `AGENTS.md` files when you have no `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in your working directory or above it. This is the default"
verdict.reason: The page supports the version (v2.1.277) and the CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md condition. In this lesson's context, though, the sentence goes further than the page. The s1-table defines "CLAUDE.md" as four locations, including `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the managed policy file. s1-concat then says all four are read together. So "CLAUDE.mdもCLAUDE.local.mdもないときに、代わりに読まれます" tells learners two wrong things: that a user or organization CLAUDE.md blocks AGENTS.md, and that AGENTS.md replaces those files. The page says the opposite: those files "don't count, and keep loading alongside AGENTS.md". The sentence also leaves out "by default", although the page says this is only the default (claude-md-or-agents-md) and the Project instructions setting can change it. The quiz explanation at line 900 does say 既定, but this definition does not. So the finding stands. The proposed fix is mostly right, but "プロジェクトに" narrows the condition too much. The page counts a CLAUDE.md in the working directory "or any directory above it", so a CLAUDE.md in a parent folder also stops AGENTS.md from being read. The fix also mentions only `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, not the managed file. The better fix below is 154 JP characters, and every sentence is 60 or fewer.

This is the default | `claude-md-and-agents-md` | Your `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` files together" (ja page: 「既定では、Claude はワーキングディレクトリまたはその上位ディレクトリに `CLAUDE.md` がない場合にのみ `AGENTS.md` を読み込みます」)
verdict.reason:
I tried to defend the card and couldn't. The memory page, in both English and Japanese, ties the no-CLAUDE.md condition to the default setting ("By default" / 「既定では」). It also names a `claude-md-and-agents-md` value for Project instructions that loads AGENTS.md alongside CLAUDE.md. The flashcard question asks「AGENTS.mdが読まれるのは？」, and its back states the default as if it were the only rule. That is stronger than the page. The lesson itself says this rule is only the default in the s4 quiz explanation (「既定では…この既定は、/config の「Project instructions」で変えられます」), but the summary card is studied on its own and leaves that out.

The card also never says where the check looks. Read at face value,「CLAUDE.mdも…ないとき」suggests that a personal ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md would block AGENTS.md. The page says that file does not count.

The v2.1.277 part is correct ("Reading AGENTS.md directly requires Claude Code v2.1.277 or later"). So is the @AGENTS.md import advice.

The proposed fix is good enough. It adds 既定では, and プロジェクトに is a fair learner-level stand-in for "working directory or above it": the troubleshooting section calls the usual cause "a CLAUDE.md somewhere on the project path", and it keeps ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md out. The fixed sentence is about 57 characters, under the 60-character limit, so no betterFix is needed.

verdict.reason: I tried to defend the lesson and could not. The official memory page does say that a path-scoped rule also loads when Claude views a matching file with a Bash command. But it only counts a command that "counts as a read", such as `cat` or `head` "on a single file". The tools reference narrows this further. Only commands on a fixed list count, each run on one file with no pipes or redirects, and "nor does any command outside this list". The lesson says 「`cat` などのコマンドで中身を見たときも同じです」 with no condition at all, and 「など」 suggests any similar command works. Under the docs, `cat a b`, `cat file | grep x`, or `less`/`awk` would not load the rule. Nothing else in the lesson adds the condition: the related flashcard at line 1051 repeats the same unqualified wording. So the lesson states this more strongly than the docs do, and the finding stands. The proposed fix 「1つのファイルを `cat` や `head` で見たときも同じです。」 copies the memory page's own wording ("such as `cat` or `head` on a single file") and is accurate. No better fix is needed.
